column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir: the plain split of a share return (yield, new shares, inflation, real growth, repricing) is how a judge can check 7.5% block by block; textbook to CFA readers, copy truncated, so quote only the identity line.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e and 3c reservoir: the method's own authors call growth and repricing its least accurate blocks, the two the top rests on; pairs with row 25; says which blocks are weak, not how weak.
Wed 18 Nov: store: US 1926-2001 blocks show about 1.5 points of history's 10.7% came from dearer shares; US only; premium figure confirmed via Song, not the truncated original.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir: the method's makers graded their own 2002 forecast too high on repricing; a past forecast graded by its authors, never a verdict on J.P. Morgan's 7.5%.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir with row 4 and Q6-016 (AQR's 2011 miss, same decade): the outcome rests on an unverified repo mirror of Shiller's data, so re-read at source and say the decade returned about twice the forecast, never too low as Keel's own grading.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e plain words: Bogle's investment return against speculative return is the clearest one-line split of 7.5%; keep the overlapping-windows caveat on the 0.81 (card Q64); US only.
Wed 18 Nov: store input for row 13: ACWI 1.61% and VT 1.60% dividend yield read at source; VT is bought in Jan 2028, so about a fifth in hand is today's yield, not hers.
Wed 18 Nov: store input for row 13: 10-year breakeven 2.20% on 16 Nov (Q10-004 holds the 6 Nov readings); never inflation risk in the report's own words (SKELETON 3e area 4).
Wed 18 Nov: store input for row 13: the IMF's 2031 growth weighted by ACWI's countries (1.89%) is Keel arithmetic; country of listing is not country of sales, as the row says.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Bernstein and Arnott's two percent dilution explains why a GDP-based block needs a deduction; read at source; the gloomy anchor of row 11.
Wed 18 Nov: store: net buybacks are the least documented block and drive most of the sum's 3.7%-6.4% spread; anchors read at source, no primary world figure, so the spread is Keel's reading.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Straehl and Ibbotson's total payouts are the counterweight to row 10; abstract and CFA review only, so cite the full paper only after reading it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir and judges' questions: today's yield, inflation and growth sum to about 5% (3.1%-6.4%), below the median of about 6.5%; Keel arithmetic, never the plan's figure and never 7.5% called wrong or too high (CANON B15, TNA frozen).
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 1 or Table 2's note: J.P. Morgan's own sentence that 7.5% is built from revenues, margins, net dilution, valuations and dividend yield, re-read at source today word for word.

Wed 18 Nov: store support for row 16: Exhibit 6 blended to ACWI; regional totals 7.5, 7.6 and 7.1 re-seen at source today, but the label mapping and the blend are Keel's, so never printed as J.P. Morgan's ACWI split.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 1 in words only (the recast 3e takes no figure there): 7.5% assumes earnings outgrow the economy, more buybacks, a weaker dollar and only a small fall in valuations; the bridge is Keel's reading from a chosen +0.2 start, never 7.5% called too high.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or Table 2's note: re-read at source today, the AI revenue lift is for U.S. large cap and in turn pushed ACWI up 50bps; say the half-point rise from 7.0% came from AI optimism on US revenues, never that the whole gap above a plain sum is a view on AI.
Wed 18 Nov: store: J.P. Morgan's -0.65% a year takes ACWI's P/E from 20.82 to about 19.5 in ten years (Keel arithmetic checked), milder than Research Affiliates or GMO; pairs with row 20.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e store with the hedge ban: the currency block is the same dollar fall IPS l.15 names (J.P. Morgan's Exhibit 4 even raises the new Taiwan dollar), but the half kept back is held in VT, so drop the half kept back, not VT; never VT as a Taiwan-dollar offset; 8q: a stronger NT$ comes with rising shares, not a larger half kept.

Wed 18 Nov: store: AQR, Research Affiliates and GMO's valuation rules quoted at source give Q6-012 (spreads come from P/E reversion beliefs) named examples; the attribution to J.P. Morgan is Keel inference, never a judgement that 7.5% is wrong.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q6b-013 (AQR 4.2% real global, about 6.5%-6.7% nominal); its new block split (yield 1.5, payout 1.6, growth 2.6, no valuation change) serves only row 13's sum; the CAPE near 29 is low-confidence inference.

Wed 18 Nov: store: GMO's own words that its forecast had run fallow or is broken add the house's self-assessment to Q6-017 and Q6-018's outside view; a past forecast, quoted, never a verdict on a live one.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 1 or 3c in words: the stated top needs VT about 3.4% a year to the move (NUMBERS 8p prints it, with 10.6% and 35.4%), below yield plus expected inflation; say no real growth in earnings per share (with -1 to -2 points of dilution and no real growth it fails), never nothing heroic, and keep 8p's 35.4% beside it; aha row 7 holds the main point.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c reservoir: the step's P/E thresholds are added (not compounded) Keel arithmetic and start from today's 20.82, but the hurdle runs from VT's January 2028 cost; restate as falls of about 1%, 4%, 7% or 9% against earnings over 2028-2031, no NUMBERS run.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and 3c reservoir, answers claim 3: over Laura's three years repricing swamps every other block (arithmetic checked: -4.7%, -8.4%, +4.9% a year); end points are illustrations from today's P/E, not January 2028's; complements Q6-024 and Q6-029.
Wed 18 Nov: writers' guard: MSCI's 20.82 and VT's 19.3x are different averages of nearly the same shares, so any P/E printed names its source; store.
Wed 18 Nov: writers' guard: VT's 19.9% earnings growth rate is five years of history on Vanguard's own page, never a forward block; never quoted as an expectation.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: the 15.64 forward P/E against 20.82 trailing implies a 33% jump the card itself flags as a likely basis difference; read MSCI's definition before any use, never quote the 33%.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e wording guard: the CFA reading's building-block approach is the risk-free rate plus premiums, so a judge trained on it hears the wrong method; say yield, growth and valuation, or name Grinold and Kroner.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Fama and French (2002) show 1951-2000 returns beat what the fundamentals gave because valuations rose; textbook, US only, working paper read.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Norway's fund ran the same sum on world shares 1970-2015 (2.5 points from repricing) and warns dividend-discount estimates are sensitive to growth; MSCI World, written 2016.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e parallel or judges' question: Diamond's 4.0-4.5 percent and the 35-45 percent real decline re-read at source today, but the MIT file is his 1999 Center for Retirement Research issue brief, so fix the APA entry; the 1998-2019 outcome rests on the unverified Shiller mirror.
Wed 18 Nov: store: FERC's two-step DCF shows a field that sets real money with the same sum and fights over g; a 3e tone parallel only, too technical for prose.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Australia's energy regulator distrusts the dividend growth model's analyst growth input; the Australian angle only if it earns its place (CLAUDE.md).
Wed 18 Nov: store: Western Australia's regulator writes a 1.0% net share creation into its formula, the public source for row 13's -1.0 anchor; twin in purpose to row 34, kept for the source.
Wed 18 Nov: store: emerging markets' faster growth reaches shareholders as a lower return in J.P. Morgan's blocks (7.1%), row 10's lesson today; one house, Keel's label mapping.

Wed 18 Nov: store: ACWI's own net return since Dec 2000 is 7.31% a year, close to 7.5% but one path ending at a high P/E; the two halvings rest on Q61, and it is never evidence the forecast will hold.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 1: NUMBERS 8p does print $18,828 at Syzygy's 5.0% against $21,179 at 7.5% and the $115,000 top, but the Wed 18 Nov recast keeps area 1 in words with no figure and the 7.5% in Table 2's note; drop the 5%, $18,800 and $21,200 from prose and keep only the basis clause.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 2's note: adding built from sales, margins, buybacks, dividends and valuations names what kind of figure 7.5% is; the note has no headroom, so only if the if-room dates item is cut; never the consensus or the top.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q6-028 (the payments never touch VT, the bottom set by Treasuries in Jan 2028, shares move only the top before the move) and aha row 7; nothing new beyond the word blocks.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or 3b: TNA l.23's two quotes re-read today; the report quotes its own note (where we allow ourselves to be wrong, already SKELETON rank 6) and evaluates it, never 7.5% was too high as a correction.
